scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: A ceiling fan makes you feel cooler, yet the room's temperature doesn't drop at all. So how does it cool you?

scenes.name: motor
scenes.text: Inside the hub, an electric motor spins the blades using magnetic fields from coils of wire.

scenes.name: blades
scenes.text: The blades are tilted at an angle, so as they spin they push air downward, like a slow propeller.

scenes.name: layer
scenes.text: Your body warms a thin layer of air around your skin. Moving air sweeps that warm blanket away.

scenes.name: sweat
scenes.text: Moving air also helps sweat evaporate faster, and evaporation pulls heat out of your skin.

scenes.name: empty
scenes.text: So a fan cools people, not rooms. Leaving it on in an empty room only wastes electricity.

scenes.name: bldc
scenes.text: Newer BLDC fans use smarter motors, and can use much less power than older fans.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Push air down, sweep heat away, speed up sweat. Follow for more on how things really work.
